title: Stow the clamp lever on an articulated light arm without moving the light
instruction: Leave the clamp lever on the light arm pointing back along the arm toward its base, without moving the light.
context: Bench technicians and product photographers set lights on articulated arms. One clamp screw at the elbow locks the arm, and its indexable lever turns the screw while seated. In a tight setup the lever is re-indexed to clear the work or a neighbouring fixture; turned the loosening way, it frees the end joint and the light drops onto the work. Unlike TK-Z5T7X3 (flip a ratchet's direction lever) and TK-D67BZ2 (tighten an arm's knob), the wrong move here silently undoes the setup.
setup: Directions are from the robot: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' is toward the left arm, heights are above the table top, the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Light arm (fixed, clamped to its base): the clamp screw's axis is vertical, 27.0 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. Base: a dark grey steel plate 90 x 70 x 10 mm centred 15 cm left of the axis, a 24 mm steel spigot to 55 mm up and a black base joint 28 x 28 x 30 mm at 45 to 75 mm. Two silver aluminium tube segments 18 mm across, centred 60 mm up, run left to right: one from 1.8 to 13.6 cm left of the axis to the base joint, one from 1.7 to 11.3 cm right of it. Elbow: a black housing 36 mm across, 40 to 80 mm up, round the axis. Clamp screw (steel, turns about the axis): a flange 26 mm across at 80 to 83 mm, a 10 x 10 mm square drive at 83 to 90 mm, a round neck 11 mm across to 112 mm and a black cap 20 mm across at 112 to 115 mm. It stands at its tight stop; it does not turn clockwise (seen from above) and turns counter-clockwise against 0.2 N m of friction. End joint: a black housing 22 mm across and 26 mm long, 12.5 cm right of the axis and 60 mm up, turning about a front-to-back axis. Light (150 g, on the end joint): a black stem 12 mm across from 65 to 95 mm up, 13.5 cm right of the axis, and a black LED panel 60 mm front to back, 95 mm left to right and 25 mm thick, its centre 17.5 cm right of the axis and 105 mm up, with a white plate on top. Clamp lever (loose, 40 g, red zinc): a square socket 20 x 20 mm outside, 12 x 12 mm inside and 8 mm deep, seated over the square drive with its underside on the flange (83 mm up), and a handle 12 mm wide and 10 mm tall from 10 to 56 mm out from the axis, ending in a round knob 14 mm across. A spring presses the lever down with 1.0 N, plus 20 N per metre it is lifted; lifted more than 7 mm it clears the drive and turns freely on the neck, and the cap stops it about 20 mm up. The end joint is held by friction from the clamp screw, 0.4 N m with the screw tight, falling to nothing at 12 degrees loose; the light's weight pulls with about 0.07 N m, so once the screw is about 10 degrees loose the light drops downward, swinging about 50 degrees toward the robot's right to the joint's stop. Lot A (the screenshot): the handle points straight away from the robot. Lot B: the handle points right, along the segment toward the light. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Pass/fail. 1.0 when, at once and for 1 second: the lever is seated on the square drive (its underside within 1.5 mm of the flange, level within 5 degrees); its handle points back along the arm toward the base, within 15 degrees; no part of either gripper is within 5 mm of the lever or the light; the lever is still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). And, over the whole trial, the light never turned more than 2 degrees on its end joint or moved more than 3 mm. Otherwise 0: the lever pointing any other way, resting on top of the drive or still held, or the light having drooped at any time, even if it was later lifted back. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Lift the lever off the square drive. 2. Turn the screw clockwise to its tight stop. 3. Lift the light back to its start, panel level, and hold it while the screw is tight. 4. Set the lever down over the drive, the handle pointing the lot's way: lot A straight away from the robot, lot B to the right along the segment toward the light. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders in PhysX. The lever's coupling is a 4-position square drive, not fine serrations. The task code applies the lever spring (1.0 N plus 20 N/m of lift), the screw's friction (0.2 N m) and the end joint's friction (0.4 N m tight, falling to zero at 12 degrees loose). Two lots stop one memorised replay, not a replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
